# Pancreatic and hepatic surgery

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Surgery > Abdominal surgery > Pancreas, liver, and bile ducts > Pancreatic and hepatic surgery*

[Original Article Link](/library/Bl0z_T)

---

## Summary

<u>Pancreatic</u> and hepatic surgeries are indicated in the management of malignant/symptomatic <u>benign tumors</u> and traumatic <u>lacerations</u> of the <u>liver</u> and <u>pancreas</u>. The choice of <u>surgery</u> depends on the location, size, and extent of the <u>malignancy</u>/injury. Depending on the extent of resection, <u>pancreatic</u> surgeries for <u>malignancy</u> include enucleation (for <u>islet cell tumors</u>), partial <u>pancreatic</u> resections (<u>distal pancreatectomy</u>, <u>central pancreatectomy</u>, <u>pancreaticoduodenectomy</u>/<u>Whipple procedure</u>), and <u>total pancreatectomy</u>. <u>Chronic pancreatitis</u> patients with a dilated <u>main pancreatic duct</u> (> 5 mm), not responding to <u>conservative therapy</u>, are candidates for <u>lateral</u> pancreaticojejunostomy with/without resection of the <u>pancreatic</u> head. Complications of <u>pancreatic</u> surgeries include <u>anastomotic leaks</u>, <u>pancreatic ascites</u>/<u>fistula</u>, and exocrine/endocrine insufficiency. Depending on which segments of the <u>liver</u> are removed, hepatic resections include right/left hepatectomy, right/left <u>lobectomy</u>, and segmentectomy. <u>Wedge resections</u> of the <u>liver</u> are performed for small, peripherally located lesions. Other complications of hepatic resections include <u>liver</u> failure, hemorrhage, <u>hemobilia</u>, and <u>bile</u> leaks.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | Type | Indications | Surgical procedure |
| <u>Pancreatic</u> resections | <br>Pancreaticoduodenectomy (<u>Whipple procedure</u>)<br> | <br><br>* Periampullary tumors  [[3]](/library/H40KkT)<br><br>* <u>Chronic pancreatitis</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Resection <br><br>* <u>Distal</u> <u>stomach</u> (<u>antrum</u> and <u>pylorus</u>)<br><br>* Entire <u>duodenum</u><br><br>* 15 cm of the <u>proximal</u> <u>jejunum</u><br><br>* Head of the <u>pancreas</u><br><br>* <u>Gall bladder</u> and the <u>CBD</u><br><br>* <u>Anastomoses</u><br><br>* Pancreaticojejunostomy<br><br>* Hepaticojejunostomy<br><br>* <u>Gastrojejunostomy</u><br><br>* Enteroenterostomy<br><br><br> |
| <br>Pylorus-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy (<u>modified Whipple procedure</u>) | <br>* Same as <u>Whipple procedure</u>  [[4]](/library/rmafSO)<br><br> | <br>* Same as <u>Whipple procedure</u>, except that the <u>distal</u> <u>stomach</u> is not resected<br><br> |  |
| <br>Distal pancreatectomy (with/without <u>splenectomy</u>) | <br>* Lesions in the body/tail of the <u>pancreas</u><br><br>* <u>Spleen</u>-preserving <u>surgery</u>: benign lesions<br><br>* With <u>splenectomy</u>: malignant/premalignant lesions<br><br> | <br><br>* The body and tail of the <u>pancreas</u> are resected, with/without the <u>spleen</u>.<br><br>* <u>Anastomosis</u>: pancreaticojejunostomy<br><br><br> |  |
| <br>Central pancreatectomy [[5]](/library/smatSO)<br> | <br><br>* Benign lesions in the neck/body of the <u>pancreas</u><br><br>* <u>Pancreatic</u> trauma<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Neck and body of the <u>pancreas</u> is resected.<br><br>* The tail is <u>anastomosed</u> to the <u>jejunum</u>.<br><br><br> |  |
| <br>Total pancreatectomy [[6]](/library/tmaXhO)<br> | <br><br>* Malignant <u>pancreatic</u> lesions<br><br>* <u>Chronic pancreatitis</u><br><br>* Multiple <u>metastasis</u> from a <u>RCC</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* The entire <u>pancreas</u>, together with the <u>duodenum</u>, is resected.<br><br>* <u>Anastomoses</u>: hepaticojejunostomy and <u>gastrojejunostomy</u><br><br>* <u>Islet cell</u> <u>autotransplantation</u><br><br><br> |  |
|  | <br>Enucleation [[7]](/library/FmaghO)<br> | <br>* <u>PNET</u> (<u>Islet cell tumors</u>)<br><br> | <br>* The <u>tumor</u> is dissected/shelled out of the surrounding normal <u>pancreatic</u> <u>parenchyma</u>.<br><br> |
| For <u>acute pancreatitis</u> | <br><u>Debridement</u> of <u>pancreatic</u> <u>parenchyma</u> (<u>Pancreatic</u> necrosectomy) [[8]](/library/8maOhO)<br> | <br><br>* Complicated <u>acute pancreatitis</u> with infected <u>necrosis</u><br><br>* Sterile <u>necrosis</u> not responding to <u>conservative therapy</u><br><br><br> | <br>* All dead and <u>necrotic</u> tissue are removed (<u>debridement</u>).<br><br> |
| For <u>chronic pancreatitis</u> | <br><u>Duodenum</u>-preserving <u>pancreatic</u> head resection (Beger procedure) [[9]](/library/umaphO)<br> | <br>* <u>Chronic pancreatitis</u> with a benign inflammatory mass in the head of the <u>pancreas</u> (not responding to <u>conservative therapy</u>).  [[10]](/library/xmaE3O)[[11]](/library/jxX_wZ0)<br><br> | <br><br>* Head of the <u>pancreas</u> is resected at the level of the <u>superior mesenteric vein</u>.<br><br>* Pancreaticojejunostomy<br><br><br> |
| <br><u>Lateral</u> pancreaticojejunostomy + resection of the <u>pancreatic</u> head (Frey procedure) | <br>* <u>Chronic pancreatitis</u> with dilated <u>main pancreatic duct</u> > 5 mm and an inflammatory mass in the head<br><br> | <br><br>* The <u>pancreatic</u> head is resected and the dilated duct is opened length wise.<br><br>* <u>Anastomosis</u>: <u>lateral</u> pancreaticojejunostomy<br><br><br> |  |
| <br><u>Lateral</u> pancreaticojejunostomy (Puestow procedure) | <br><br>* <u>Chronic pancreatitis</u> with a dilated <u>main pancreatic duct</u> > 5 mm without an inflammatory mass in the head [[9]](/library/umaphO)<br><br>* <u>Pancreas divisum</u> with dilated <u>main pancreatic duct</u><br><br><br> | <br>* Same as Frey's procedure, but without the <u>pancreatic</u> head resection<br><br> |  |
| For <u>pancreatic pseudocysts</u> | <br><u>Pseudocyst</u>-gastrostomy (cystogastrostomy) <u>Pseudocyst</u>-duodenostomy (cystoduodenostomy) <u>Pseudocyst</u>-<u>jejunostomy</u> (cystojejunostomy) | <br>* Complicated or symptomatic <u>pseudocysts</u> (see <u>pancreatic pseudocysts</u>)<br><br> | <br>* The cyst is drained into the <u>stomach</u>, <u>duodenum</u> or <u>jejunum</u><br><br> |
| For <u>pancreatic fistulae</u> | <br>Fistulojejunostomy <u>Pancreatic</u> resection (e.g., <u>distal pancreatectomy</u> for <u>distal</u> duct disruption) [[3]](/library/H40KkT)<br> | <br>* Failure of conservative and endoscopic management  [[12]](/library/vmaAhO)<br><br> | <br><br>* Fistulojejunostomy: The fistulous tract is excised up until the <u>pancreatic</u> origin; a loop of <u>jejunum</u> is then sutured to the affected part of the <u>pancreas</u>.<br><br>* <u>Distal pancreatectomy</u>: see above<br><br><br> |

### Complications




* <u>Delayed gastric emptying</u>/<u>gastroparesis</u> (most common)  [[13]](/library/9maN3O)[[14]](/library/Cmaq3O)

* Pancreaticojejunostomy <u>anastomotic leak</u>/<u>pancreatic</u> ductal disruption → leakage of <u>pancreatic</u> secretions into the <u>abdominal cavity</u> which leads to: 

* <u>Hyperchloremic</u> <u>acidosis</u>

* <u>Pancreatic fistula</u>

* <u>Pancreatic pseudocyst</u>

* <u>Pancreatic ascites</u>

* Hepaticojejunostomy <u>anastomotic leak</u> → biliary <u>peritonitis</u>

* <u>Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency</u>  [[14]](/library/Cmaq3O)

* Endocrine <u>pancreatic</u> insufficiency (<u>diabetes mellitus</u>) and lifelong dependence on <u>insulin</u>

* <u>Small bowel obstruction</u>: <u>herniation</u>, <u>volvulus</u>, <u>anastomotic stricture</u>

* <u>Intraabdominal abscess</u> or <u>sepsis</u>

* <u>Gastrointestinal hemorrhage</u>

* If the <u>duodenum</u> is resected: <u>iron deficiency anemia</u>





> [!NOTE]
> Suspect a pancreaticojejunostomy <u>anastomotic leak</u> in a patient with <u>hyperchloremic</u> <u>acidosis</u> (loss of <u>bicarbonate</u>) and high levels of <u>amylase</u> in abdominal secretions.

## Hepatic surgery

### Anatomy of the <u>liver</u>



* See “<u>Liver</u>.”




### General principles of <u>hepatic surgery</u>




* Access: <u>laparotomy</u> (transverse, midline or subcostal <u>incisions</u>) or <u>laparoscopy</u>

* Pringle maneuver: temporary occlusion of the hepatic <u>artery</u> and <u>portal vein</u> by clamping of the free edge of the <u>lesser omentum</u> (<u>hepatoduodenal ligament</u>) in order to control vascular inflow to the <u>liver</u> or to reduce hemorrhage

* <u>Cholecystectomy</u> is routinely performed as part of all major hepatic resections to allow for easier dissection during the <u>surgery</u>.

* Cavitron ultrasonic surgical aspirator (CUSA): uses ultrasonic waves to vaporize only the <u>liver</u> cells while sparing the biliary radicles and <u>blood vessels</u>





![Pringle Maneuver](media/i6737290eaw7cnqcvx6xg7bj.jpg)

Pringle Maneuver




### Types of <u>liver</u> resections [[15]](/library/sfYtno)




| Overview of <u>liver</u> resection types |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | Type | Indications | Contraindications | Surgical procedure |
| <br>Anatomical resections<br> | <br>Right hepatectomy (right hemihepatectomy) | <br><br>* <u>Hepatocellular carcinoma</u><br><br>* Secondary <u>metastasis</u> in the <u>liver</u> (e.g., <u>metastasis</u> from <u>colorectal carcinoma</u>, <u>neuroendocrine tumors</u>)<br><br>* Symptomatic <u>benign liver tumors</u> (<u>focal nodular hyperplasia</u>, <u>hepatic hemangioma</u>, <u>hepatocellular adenoma</u>)<br><br>* Symptomatic  <u>hepatic cysts</u><br><br>* Deep <u>liver</u> <u>lacerations</u> or <u>parenchymal</u> avulsions  [[16]](/library/AmaRRO)<br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Child class C</u> <u>liver cirrhosis</u><br><br>* Low future <u>liver</u> remnant (FLR)  [[17]](/library/ymadRO)<br><br>* <u>Child class B</u> <u>liver cirrhosis</u> with FLR < 40%<br><br>* <u>Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis</u> with FLR < 30%<br><br><br> | <br>* Segments V, VI, VII, and, VIII are removed.<br><br> |
| <br>* Right hepatectomy and the additional removal of segments I and IV<br><br> |  |  |  |  |
| Left hepatectomy | <br>* Segments II, III, and IV are removed.<br><br> |  |  |  |
| Left <u>lobectomy</u> | <br>* Segments II and III are removed (<u>liver</u> to the left of the <u>falciform ligament</u>).<br><br> |  |  |  |
| Segmental resection |  |  | <br>* One or more anatomical segments are removed.<br><br> |  |
| <br>Non-anatomical resection <br> | <u>Wedge resection</u> | <br>* Peripherally located lesions<br><br> |  | <br>* A triangular wedge of hepatic <u>parenchyma</u> containing the lesion is removed.<br><br> |





### Complications




* Hemorrhage

* <u>Hemobilia</u>  [[18]](/library/zmarRO)[[19]](/library/PxXW9Z0)

* <u>Bile</u> leak

* <u>Liver</u> failure





> [!NOTE]
> Before performing extensive hepatic resections the future <u>liver</u> remnant (FLR) needs to be calculated (using CT images), as patients with insufficient FLR postresection, can develop <u>liver</u> failure.
